overview: This file traces two related postal-policy issues concerning Japan from the final months of the Second World War into the Allied occupation. A 1945 cross-reference records a Japanese decision to raise railway fares and postal rates, while two documents from January 1947 address the territorial meaning of “Japan” for postal service. The latter reproduce the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers’ detailed definition of the islands included in and excluded from Japan and show the Civil Affairs Division, State Department, and Post Office Department coordinating its application.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram no. 810 on Japanese railway and postal rate increases
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a telegram reporting that Japan planned to increase railway ticket prices and postal rates from April 1.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet points to telegram no. 810, dated February 5, 1945, concerning a decision by the Japanese communications ministry to increase railway fares and postal charges effective April 1. The original document was filed under number 894.773/2-545 rather than retained here. The form identifies Bern as the destination but does not identify the sender.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Mrs. Buckley on the postal definition of Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum concludes that no further State Department action is needed concerning the definition of Japan for postal purposes.
subfiles.summary: Lewis informs Buckley that the relevant offices and the Post Office Department have already discussed the issue. He notes that the Post Office Department possesses the information contained in the Civil Affairs Division’s letter. The memorandum therefore recommends no further action.

subfiles.title: Civil Affairs Division letter defining Japan for postal purposes
subfiles.from: Major General Daniel Noce, Chief, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: Assistant Secretary of State J. H. Hilldring, attention G. W. Lewis
subfiles.about: The Civil Affairs Division transmits SCAP’s territorial definition of Japan and recommends its use in Post Office Department orders governing postal service.
subfiles.summary: Noce reports that a SCAP reply received on January 23, 1947, defined Japan for postal purposes by reference to SCAPIN 677 as modified by SCAPIN 841. The letter reproduces a detailed definition that includes Japan’s four main islands and specified adjacent islands while excluding Korea-associated islands, southern Ryukyu and Nanpō islands, several Pacific island groups, and the Kuril, Habomai, and Shikotan islands. Noce recommends forwarding the definition to the Post Office Department so that it can delimit postal service with Japan.

interest: The file is useful for showing how seemingly routine postal administration became entangled with the unsettled territorial geography of postwar Japan. The Civil Affairs Division letter preserves a compact contemporary statement of SCAP’s administrative boundaries, including numerous exonyms, Japanese names, and now-obsolete or disputed designations. Together with the brief internal memorandum, it also documents how military occupation authorities, diplomats, and postal officials translated occupation directives into ordinary government practice.
